children: Inflation in the Philippines accelerated in September as fuel and food prices rose, ahead of the central bank's interest-rate decision later this month.

The consumer-price index for September rose 7.2% compared with the same period a year earlier, picking up from August's 6.1% increase, data from the Philippine Statistics Authority showed Tuesday. The increase was the fastest pace since April, when it also rose 7.2%.
Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas had forecast inflation of 6.4%-7.4% for September, while the median forecast from a Wall Street Journal poll was 6.8%.
Core inflation, which excludes selected food and energy items, accelerated to 4.7% in September from 4.1% in August.

The rise in overall inflation was mainly due to the faster annual gains in the heavily-weighted food and non-alcoholic beverages index, the PSA said. The housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels index as well as the transport index also lifted September's inflation, it added.
Inflation averaged 5.4% in the first nine months of the year.
Rising global oil prices continue to threaten the Philippines' inflation outlook, given its heavy reliance on supplies from the Middle East.
El Nino could also further push up food prices, as the hot, dry conditions it brings threaten crop production.
The central bank next meets on Oct. 22. It raised its policy rate to 5.00% in August to guard against inflation risks from a severe El Nino event and larger-than-expected wage increases.
Food's large share of the consumer-price basket leaves inflation and household spending sensitive to rising food prices, ANZ Research analysts said in a recent report.
High food inflation and weak domestic demand complicate the central bank's policy decisions, ANZ added. It expects one more quarter-percentage-point rate increase this quarter.
"That said, the threshold for additional tightening remains high, given the soft growth backdrop," ANZ added.
